section: Energy efficiency - Bureau of Energy Efficiency, Energy Conservation Act, PAT scheme, star labelling, UJALA
subsections: Standards and labelling - star label, mandatory vs voluntary, rating scale
PAT scheme - designated consumers, cycles, ESCerts
Building codes - ECO Niwas Samhita, ECSBC

accepted.s: The Standards and Labelling programme for energy-consuming equipment in India is administered by which organisation under which Ministry?
o: National Productivity Council under the Ministry of Heavy Industries
Energy Efficiency Services Limited under the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy
Bureau of Energy Efficiency under the Ministry of Power
Central Electricity Authority under the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
accepted.x: The Standards and Labelling programme is administered by the Bureau of Energy Efficiency under the Ministry of Power.
accepted.tq: Identify the organisation and parent ministry without confusing neighbouring energy institutions.
accepted.sec: Standards and labelling - star label, mandatory vs voluntary, rating scale  [other exams]

accepted.s: The Standards and Labelling programme was launched in which year?
accepted.x: The Standards and Labelling programme was launched in 2006.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the programme-launch year from the years associated with the Energy Conservation Act and PAT.
accepted.sec: Standards and labelling - star label, mandatory vs voluntary, rating scale  [other exams]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Bureau of Energy Efficiency's Standards and Labelling programme:
1. It covers more than 40 types of equipment.
2. Its rating scale ranges from one star to five stars.
3. Each additional star saves approximately 10–15 per cent energy.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The programme covers more than 40 equipment categories, uses a one-to-five-star scale and each additional star is associated with approximately 10–15 per cent energy savings.
accepted.tq: Use the quantitative and scale clues together; all three statements are supported.
accepted.sec: Standards and labelling - star label, mandatory vs voluntary, rating scale  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is a voluntary category under the Standards and Labelling programme?
accepted.x: General-purpose industrial motors are listed under the voluntary category, whereas refrigerators, fans and washing machines are mandatory examples.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the mandatory and voluntary lists rather than selecting a familiar labelled appliance.
accepted.sec: Standards and labelling - star label, mandatory vs voluntary, rating scale  [other exams]

accepted.s:
Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched with the mandatory category under the Standards and Labelling programme?
1. Induction hob
2. Solar inverter
3. Computer
4. Domestic LPG stove
accepted.x: Computers are given as a voluntary example. Induction hobs, solar inverters and domestic LPG stoves are listed as mandatory examples.
accepted.tq: Find the single item transferred from the voluntary list into the mandatory list.
accepted.sec: Standards and labelling - star label, mandatory vs voluntary, rating scale  [other exams]

accepted.s:
With effect from 1 January 2026, star labelling became mandatory, having earlier been voluntary, for which of the following groups?
1. Refrigerators and televisions
2. LPG stoves and cooling towers
3. Chillers and deep freezers
4. Distribution transformers and grid-connected solar inverters
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: From 1 January 2026, mandatory labelling was extended to all the listed categories, which had earlier been voluntary.
accepted.tq: Check the complete date-linked list; the correct option contains every listed category.
accepted.sec: Standards and labelling - star label, mandatory vs voluntary, rating scale  [other exams]

accepted.s: Under the star-labelling changes effective from 1 January 2026, manufacturers may be penalised when:
o: the product receives fewer than three stars irrespective of its actual consumption
actual energy consumption deviates from the declared label rating
a product is sold without an international energy certificate
the product is manufactured outside a designated consumer sector
accepted.x: Manufacturers may be penalised if the actual energy consumption of a product deviates from the consumption declared through its label.
accepted.tq: Apply the compliance rule to a manufacturer’s conduct instead of confusing rating level with accuracy of declaration.
accepted.sec: Standards and labelling - star label, mandatory vs voluntary, rating scale  [other exams]

accepted.s: The Perform, Achieve and Trade (PAT) scheme is best described as:
o: a voluntary household scheme for purchasing energy-efficient appliances
a carbon-offset scheme limited to residential buildings
a tax-based scheme for replacing all fossil-fuel plants with nuclear plants
a market mechanism that sets energy-reduction targets for designated consumers
accepted.x: PAT is a market mechanism under NMEEE that assigns energy-reduction targets to designated consumers.
accepted.tq: Match the scheme with its operative mechanism and target group.
accepted.sec: PAT scheme - designated consumers, cycles, ESCerts  [other exams]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about Energy Saving Certificates (ESCerts) under PAT:
1. Designated consumers that over-achieve their targets can earn ESCerts.
2. Designated consumers that fail to achieve their targets may buy ESCerts.
3. ESCerts are traded on power exchanges.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Over-achievers earn ESCerts, under-achievers buy them, and the certificates are traded on power exchanges, including the Indian Energy Exchange.
accepted.tq: Track the market mechanism through its three linked stages: earning, buying and trading.
accepted.sec: PAT scheme - designated consumers, cycles, ESCerts  [other exams]

accepted.s: PAT Cycle I, launched for the period 2012–15, covered:
accepted.x: PAT Cycle I covered 478 units in eight sectors during 2012–15.
accepted.tq: Separate PAT cycle figures from the later ADEETIE figures and the future residual-sector arrangement.
accepted.sec: PAT scheme - designated consumers, cycles, ESCerts  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which one of the following was NOT included among the original PAT sectors?
accepted.x: The original PAT sectors included thermal power, chlor-alkali and textiles. Railways was added later and is part of the proposed residual-sector arrangement.
accepted.tq: Use the time qualifier to distinguish original sectors from sectors added later.
accepted.sec: PAT scheme - designated consumers, cycles, ESCerts  [other exams]

accepted.s:
Which of the following correctly represents the original PAT sectors?
1. Iron and steel
2. Cement
3. Aluminium
4. Fertilisers
5. Petrochemicals
6. Pulp and paper
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Iron and steel, cement, aluminium, fertilisers, petrochemicals and pulp and paper were among the original PAT sectors. The original list also included thermal power, chlor-alkali and textiles.
accepted.tq: Reconstruct the sector list by checking every listed industry rather than relying on one familiar example.
accepted.sec: PAT scheme - designated consumers, cycles, ESCerts  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs correctly distinguishes PAT from CCTS?
o: PAT applies only to households, whereas CCTS applies only to agriculture
PAT issues energy-intensity certificates, whereas CCTS issues emission-intensity certificates
PAT issues carbon compliance certificates, whereas CCTS issues energy-intensity certificates
Both PAT and CCTS issue only renewable-energy certificates
accepted.x: PAT is associated with energy-intensity certificates, called ESCerts, while CCTS is associated with emission-intensity certificates, called CCCs.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between two similar market mechanisms by their certificate type.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: After the expansion of the Carbon Credit Trading Scheme (CCTS), PAT is proposed to retain which four residual sectors?
o: Chlor-alkali, cement, railways and domestic buildings
Iron and steel, petrochemicals, refineries and pulp and paper
Thermal power, railways, DISCOMs and commercial buildings
accepted.x: The proposed four residual PAT sectors are thermal power, railways, DISCOMs and commercial buildings.
accepted.tq: Use the future-sector list as a direct four-item recall question and reject the older industrial grouping.
accepted.sec: PAT scheme - designated consumers, cycles, ESCerts  [other exams]

accepted.s: PAT is associated with which of the following initiatives?
o: National Mission for Enhanced Energy Efficiency under the National Action Plan on Climate Change
National Solar Mission under the Ministry of Finance
Smart Cities Mission under the Ministry of Power
National Mission for Sustainable Agriculture under the National Action Plan on Climate Change
accepted.x: PAT operates under the National Mission for Enhanced Energy Efficiency (NMEEE), which is one of the missions under NAPCC.
accepted.tq: Match the programme with its correct mission and policy framework.
accepted.sec: PAT scheme - designated consumers, cycles, ESCerts  [other exams]

accepted.s: The Bureau of Energy Efficiency became operational on:
accepted.x: BEE became operational on 1 March 2002.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the operational date from the enactment year of the Energy Conservation Act and the launch year of Standards and Labelling.
accepted.sec: BEE - statutory basis, parent ministry

accepted.s: The National Mission for Enhanced Energy Efficiency is one of how many missions under the National Action Plan on Climate Change?
accepted.x: NMEEE is one of the eight missions under NAPCC, established in 2008.
accepted.tq: Use the exact mission count rather than confusing it with the number of PAT sectors or ADEETIE sectors.
accepted.sec: BEE - statutory basis, parent ministry

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly states the reported results of energy-efficiency initiatives in FY 2023–24?
o: 321.06 MT of CO2 avoided annually and 53.6 Mtoe saved
53.6 million tonnes of CO2 avoided and 321.06 Mtoe saved
321.06 million tonnes of CO2 avoided and 53.6 Mtoe saved
80 million tonnes of CO2 avoided and 14 Mtoe saved
accepted.x: The reported results were 321.06 million tonnes of CO2 avoided annually and 53.6 Mtoe of energy saved in FY 2023–24.
accepted.tq: Check both the unit and the order of the two figures; the reversed pair is the key trap.
accepted.sec: BEE - statutory basis, parent ministry

accepted.s: ADEETIE, launched in July 2025 with an outlay of ₹1,000 crore, primarily focuses on:
o: star labelling of household refrigerators only
carbon trading by state governments only
energy generation in nuclear power plants
accepted.x: ADEETIE focuses on energy efficiency among micro, small and medium enterprises through audits and financial support.
accepted.tq: Identify the programme’s target group rather than its funding or implementation details.
accepted.sec: BEE - statutory basis, parent ministry

accepted.s: Under ADEETIE, the interest subvention rates are:
o: 5% for all MSMEs irrespective of category
3% for micro and small enterprises and 5% for medium enterprises
5% for micro and small enterprises and 3% for medium enterprises
10% for micro enterprises and 5% for small enterprises
accepted.x: ADEETIE provides a 5 per cent interest subvention for micro and small enterprises and 3 per cent for medium enterprises.
accepted.tq: Compare the two adjacent rates and associate the higher rate with micro and small enterprises.
accepted.sec: BEE - statutory basis, parent ministry

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes the coverage of ADEETIE?
accepted.x: ADEETIE covers 60 clusters across 14 sectors.
accepted.tq: Keep the cluster figure and sector figure in their correct order and distinguish them from PAT Cycle I data.
accepted.sec: BEE - statutory basis, parent ministry

accepted.s:
Which of the following is NOT listed as a programme or activity associated with BEE?
1. State Energy Efficiency Index
2. PAT
3. Standards and Labelling
4. ECBC
5. CAFE and NECA
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: SEEI, PAT, Standards and Labelling, ECBC, CAFE and NECA are all associated with BEE. Therefore none of the listed items is the exception.
accepted.tq: Test the EXCEPT structure by verifying every programme against the BEE programme set.
accepted.sec: BEE - statutory basis, parent ministry

accepted.s: The principal objective of BEE programmes such as PAT, Standards and Labelling and ECBC is to:
o: restrict energy use to industrial consumers
reduce the energy intensity of the economy
increase the energy intensity of the economy
accepted.x: These programmes aim to reduce the energy intensity of the economy.
accepted.tq: Infer the common policy objective from the functions of the programmes.
accepted.sec: BEE - statutory basis, parent ministry

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below.
List-I (Code)
a. ECBC
b. ECO Niwas Samhita
c. ECSBC
List-II (Scope or feature)
i. Residential buildings
 ii. New commercial buildings
 iii. Sustainability added to the energy-conservation building framework

Code:
a  b  c
1. i  ii  iii
2. ii  i  iii
3. ii  iii  i
4. iii  i  ii
accepted.x: ECBC applies to new commercial buildings, ECO Niwas Samhita applies to residential buildings, and ECSBC adds sustainability to the framework.
accepted.tq: Start with the sure pair: ECO Niwas Samhita is the residential-building code.
accepted.sec: Building codes - ECO Niwas Samhita, ECSBC

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about building energy codes:
1. ECBC was introduced in 2007 for new commercial buildings.
2. Buildings complying with ECBC use approximately 25–40 per cent less energy.
3. ECO Niwas Samhita was introduced in 2018 for residential buildings.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct: ECBC dates from 2007, applies to new commercial buildings and can reduce energy use by about 25–40 per cent; ECO Niwas Samhita dates from 2018 and covers residential buildings.
accepted.tq: Combine date, scope and quantitative-effect statements in one coded question.
accepted.sec: Building codes - ECO Niwas Samhita, ECSBC

accepted.s: The Energy Conservation and Sustainable Building Code (ECSBC) is associated with which year?
accepted.x: ECSBC is associated with 2024 and follows the 2022 amendment; it adds sustainability to the ECBC framework.
accepted.tq: Separate the code’s publication year from the year of the amendment that preceded it.
accepted.sec: Building codes - ECO Niwas Samhita, ECSBC

accepted.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: ECO Niwas Samhita — new commercial buildings — 2007
ECSBC — sustainability-oriented building code after the 2022 amendment — 2024
accepted.x: ECSBC is the 2024 sustainability-oriented building code following the 2022 amendment. ECBC concerns new commercial buildings, while ECO Niwas Samhita concerns residential buildings.
accepted.tq: Check both the scope and year in each pair; the correct pair preserves both dimensions.
accepted.sec: Building codes - ECO Niwas Samhita, ECSBC

accepted.s: The Andhra Pradesh model Super ECBC building referred to in the context of energy-efficient construction is located at:
accepted.x: The AP model Super ECBC building is located at Sagar Nagar in Visakhapatnam.
accepted.tq: Use the location clue to distinguish the AP example from other possible urban energy-efficiency sites.
accepted.sec: Building codes - ECO Niwas Samhita, ECSBC

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes the significance of energy efficiency in India?
o: It eliminates the need for all new energy sources immediately.
It can reduce demand and emissions and strengthen energy security in a country dependent on imports for about 80% of its oil.
It is generally the most expensive route to reduce demand and emissions.
It affects only the building sector and has no relation to energy security.
accepted.x: Energy efficiency is a relatively inexpensive route to reduce demand and emissions and improves energy security, particularly given India’s approximately 80 per cent oil-import dependence.
accepted.tq: Apply the significance statement to both emissions reduction and energy security.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with its first-in-category distinction?
o: APSECM — India’s first carbon credit exchange
CCTS — India’s first mandatory compliance carbon market
UJALA — India’s first mandatory compliance carbon market
PAT — India’s first standalone State Designated Agency
accepted.x: CCTS is described as India’s first mandatory compliance carbon market, while APSECM is the first standalone State Designated Agency.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between two different FIRST/LAST distinctions rather than combining them.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: APSECM is significant in Andhra Pradesh because it is:
o: the first standalone State Designated Agency
the first power exchange for ESCerts
the first nuclear-energy regulator in the State
accepted.x: APSECM is identified as the first standalone State Designated Agency in Andhra Pradesh and has also been associated with Front Runner status in 2018 and the first NECA prize.
accepted.tq: Match the institution with its distinctive first rather than with a related national programme.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s:
Which of the following statements about Andhra Pradesh’s energy-efficiency initiatives is/are correct?
1. APSECM was a Front Runner in 2018.
2. APSECM received the first prize under NECA.
3. The 15th Executive Committee of APSECM reviewed DSM, ECBC, PAT and Standards and Labelling.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: All three statements are correct: APSECM was a 2018 Front Runner, received the first NECA prize, and its 15th Executive Committee reviewed DSM, ECBC, PAT and Standards and Labelling.
accepted.tq: Link the State-specific distinction, award and committee agenda without substituting a national institution.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: Which of the following events is correctly associated with its date?
o: Launch of the Standards and Labelling programme — 2012
accepted.x: BEE became operational on 1 March 2002. The Standards and Labelling programme began in 2006, ECO Niwas Samhita dates from 2018, and PAT Cycle I ran from 2012 to 2015.
accepted.tq: Separate closely related institutional, programme and code dates before selecting the correctly matched pair.
accepted.sec: BEE - statutory basis, parent ministry
